title: Advancing cortisol measurements in zebrafish using a commercial ELISA kit
author: Jorge, Félix, et al.
materials: 1.Cut fish trunks with an ophthalmologic scissor (Dentalhonest, Chengdu, China) in 500 µL PBS.2.Homogenize trunk samples by bead beating (five 3 mm steal beads) in the FastPrepⓇ−24 (MP Biomedicals, Solon, Ohio, United States of America; 6 m/s) for 60 s at room temperature.3.Vortex skin mucus samples (Reagente 5 vortex mixer - Química E Electrónica, Lda., Porto, Portugal) for 2 min at a speed of 35 Hz.4.Add to each trunk sample 750 µL of methanol (HPLC grade 99.8%; Fisher Scientific, Loughborough, United Kingdom).5.Add 500 or 2000 µL methanol to each skin mucus samples with 5 or 10 fish's cotton tips, respectively.6.Keep all samples (trunk and skin mucus) in a lab roller (built in-house according to Dhankani and Pearce [23]) at 60 rpm for 24 h at room temperature.7.Centrifuge (Centrifuge 5415 R, Eppendorf, Hamburg, Germany) samples at 10,000 g for 10 min at 4 °C.8.Discard the swabs of the skin mucus samples and transfer the supernatant of all samples (trunk and skin mucus) to new microcentrifuge tubes.9.Evaporate tubes at 36 °C on a vacuum concentrator (Savant™ SPD131DDA SpeedVac™ Concentrator, ThermoScientific Inc., Waltham, Massachusetts, United States of America).10.Reconstitute cortisol volume of the trunk samples with 500 µL PBS.11.Reconstitute the volume of skin mucus samples according to the assay test: 125 µL for the specificity test and 260 µL for the precision and accuracy test.12.Keep all samples overnight at 4 °C.13.Add 500 µL n-Hexane (97+%; Acros Organics, Geel, Belgium) to trunk samples to remove the interference of precipitated lipids. After 15 min of freezing at −20 °C, discard the organic layer of these samples.

steps.title: Cut fish trunks in PBS
steps.instruction: Cut fish trunks with an ophthalmologic scissor (Dentalhonest, Chengdu, China) and place them in 500 µL phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS).

steps.title: Homogenize trunk samples by bead beating
steps.instruction: Homogenize each trunk sample by bead beating using five 3 mm steel beads in a FastPrep®‑24 (MP Biomedicals, Solon, OH; 6 m/s) for 60 s at room temperature.

steps.title: Vortex skin mucus samples
steps.instruction: Vortex skin‑mucus samples with a Reagente 5 vortex mixer (Química E Electrónica, Lda., Porto, Portugal) for 2 min at 35 Hz.

steps.title: Add methanol to trunk samples
steps.instruction: Add 750 µL of HPLC‑grade methanol (99.8 %; Fisher Scientific, Loughborough, UK) to each trunk sample.

steps.title: Add methanol to skin mucus samples
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL methanol to skin‑mucus samples collected with 5 fish cotton tips, or 2000 µL methanol to samples collected with 10 fish cotton tips.

steps.title: Incubate samples on roller
steps.instruction: Place all trunk and skin‑mucus samples in a laboratory roller (built in‑house per Dhankani and Pearce [23]) set to 60 rpm and incubate for 24 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Centrifuge samples
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the samples in a Centrifuge 5415 R (Eppendorf, Hamburg, Germany) at 10 000 g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to new tubes
steps.instruction: Discard the cotton swabs from the skin‑mucus samples and transfer the supernatant from all samples (trunk and skin‑mucus) into fresh microcentrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Evaporate samples in SpeedVac
steps.instruction: Evaporate the tubes at 36 °C using a Savant™ SPD131DDA SpeedVac™ Concentrator (ThermoScientific, Waltham, MA).

steps.title: Reconstitute trunk samples in PBS
steps.instruction: Reconstitute each trunk sample with 500 µL PBS.

steps.title: Reconstitute skin mucus samples per assay
steps.instruction: Reconstitute skin‑mucus samples with 125 µL for the specificity test or 260 µL for the precision and accuracy test, as required by the assay.

steps.title: Store samples overnight at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Keep all reconstituted samples at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Extract lipids with n‑Hexane and discard layer
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL n‑hexane (97 + %; Acros Organics, Geel, Belgium) to each trunk sample, freeze for 15 min at –20 °C, then discard the organic (hexane) layer.

steps.title: Add standards/samples to ELISA plate
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL of standards or samples (DetectX® kit, Arbor Assays, K003‑H1) to each well of the microplate in duplicate.

steps.title: Add cortisol conjugate and antibody
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL of cortisol conjugate and antibody mixture to each well.

steps.title: Tap plate three times
steps.instruction: Tap the plate three times to mix the contents.

steps.title: Incubate plate in dark
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate in the dark for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash plate with buffer
steps.instruction: Discard the liquid and add 200 µL wash buffer to each well.

steps.title: Repeat wash three times with tapping
steps.instruction: Repeat the wash step three additional times, tapping the plate on absorbent paper after each wash.

steps.title: Add TMB substrate solution
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 3,3′,5,5′‑tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) substrate solution to each well.

steps.title: Incubate plate post‑substrate
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate for 30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Add stop solution
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL stop solution to each well.

steps.title: Read plate at 450/490 nm
steps.instruction: Read the plate at 450 nm and 490 nm, 25 °C, using a PowerWave XS2 microplate scanner (Bio‑Tek Instruments, Winooski, VT) with Gen5 analysis software.

steps.title: Calculate bounded cortisol concentrations
steps.instruction: Calculate bounded cortisol by dividing the mean absorbance of each duplicate (or of each standard, B) by the absorbance of the zero‑cortisol well (B₀); express results in nanograms per deciliter (ng/dL).

description: The DetectXⓇ assay was validated using fundamental criteria for analytical validation: precision, specificity, accuracy, and sensitivity [21]. However, the sensitivity, which is the lowest level of cortisol that the assay kit is capable of detecting, was not calculated, as the manufacturer had already estimated it to be 0.00276 µg/dL.
